data.name: Ighrast Salt League
data.short_lore: The Ighrast clans carry pale salt from the southern pans to the river cities, and their oasis wells are the only water for three hundred leagues. Honour binds their hosts tighter than any castle wall. Now the river-guild's salt tariffs and the Regency's tolls at Iggoudar anger the clans, and raiders ride from Tassemmar toward the Ouarnast wharves.

towns.name: Tassemmar
towns.blurb: Salt-weighing city whose brass scales set the weight for every caravan contract.

towns.name: Ahnarou
towns.blurb: Oasis market where date groves feed caravans before the long waste crossing.

towns.name: Imzellan
towns.blurb: Walled well-town; its Dry Gate shuts each year on the first sandstorm of autumn.

towns.name: Tizgadeen
towns.blurb: Tanners' quarter famed for indigo veils, and a feud with the Regency over tolls.

towns.name: Ouarnast
towns.blurb: Wharf town on the salt lake; rival caravans duel for the first place at the loading ramp.

towns.name: Zerhalan
towns.blurb: Lantern city of the eastern oasis; the emir's hall hosts any guest for three days.

castles.name: Azzenwar
castles.blurb: Hilltop well-fort guarding the only spring on the northern salt road.

castles.name: Tahnoun
castles.blurb: Mud-brick keep where the clans hold their oath-moots under the stars.

castles.name: Iggoudar
castles.blurb: Toll-castle at the river ford; its garrison has fought the Regency for a decade.

castles.name: Amrash
castles.blurb: Watchtower of pale stone where lookouts signal raids by mirror and smoke.

castles.name: Irhessa
castles.blurb: Ruined fort said to be built by the first salt-kings, haunted by their camels.

castles.name: Ouallen
castles.blurb: Strong gatehouse over the caravan route; any lancer who passes owes it a song.

castles.name: Ghaddun
castles.blurb: Fortress of the shade-wells; its stores of dates and water feed besieged hosts.

castles.name: Tinsada
castles.blurb: Cliff-hold on the red escarpment, reachable only by a single winding stair.

castles.name: Sidrait
castles.blurb: Lancer barracks with stables for a thousand horses and a long feud with the Fen.

villages.name: Iddrin
villages.blurb: Date-farmers' hamlet known for the sweetest fruit in the south.

villages.name: Tamzerat
villages.blurb: Well village where a legend says the first camel knelt to drink.

villages.name: Ahlouf
villages.blurb: Tent-camp that moves with the seasons and never shows its walls twice.

villages.name: Essidra
villages.blurb: Salt-pan village; its workers sing a grudge against river-guild buyers.

villages.name: Unzal
villages.blurb: Dust-bowl hamlet of goatherds, famous for its rough wine of figs.

villages.name: Tifrasht
villages.blurb: Shrine-spring where caravaners leave a coin and a promise for safe passage.

villages.name: Imzaz
villages.blurb: Mint village that stamps the clans' silver tokens for trade.

villages.name: Anhilt
villages.blurb: Hamlet of tanners who cure hides for the lancers' saddles and boots.

villages.name: Tazirda
villages.blurb: Horse-breeding village whose grey mares are prized across the continent.

villages.name: Ouzmar
villages.blurb: Quarry hamlet cutting pale stone for the few castles the clans raise.

villages.name: Ifghelen
villages.blurb: Oasis village with a sunken garden said to hold a sleeping spirit.

villages.name: Tinouzat
villages.blurb: Shepherd village; its herders still nurse the grudge of a stolen flock.

villages.name: Ahnazz
villages.blurb: Caravanserai village where a neutral oath is sworn over a bowl of salt.

villages.name: Irzaghen
villages.blurb: Mud village built on the bones of a raided fort, a warning to raiders.

villages.name: Tahassal
villages.blurb: Village of falconers whose birds hunt the Fen's reed-geese each autumn.

villages.name: Ilmadd
villages.blurb: Lamp village known for oil pressed from desert seeds and sold in the towns.

villages.name: Azgrar
villages.blurb: Border hamlet where the clans hand over tolls and taxes to Regency men.

villages.name: Essaghen
villages.blurb: Herding camp famous for its water songs, sung at every well-blessing.

villages.name: Tiwerz
villages.blurb: Village of weavers whose striped cloaks mark a clan's rank on the road.

villages.name: Ouhrat
villages.blurb: Gate village; its headman judges raids and sets the price of blood.

villages.name: Tamrazh
villages.blurb: Last village before the waste; a cairn marks each caravan lost beyond it.
